source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including all written/read and other notes, not normalized reconstructions.
source.public_versification_note: Public Joshua 18–24 and Hebrew source references align one to one. All 216 original source records are bound exactly once.

key_decisions.decision: Retain ancestors’ other-god service and the opening of a divine first-person historical speech; explain River selectively.
Keep shifts between ancestors and you, full military equipment and Hebrew sea designation.
Retain third-person LORD/he within divine first-person speech and the later return to I rather than silently harmonizing speakers.
Preserve human fighting, divine giving and destruction and resulting possession.
Keep fought against as this account’s characterization rather than harmonizing it with another narrative.
Keep Jericho’s people and all seven named peoples as the retrospective account presents them.
Preserve hornet, two kings and denial of weapon agency without harmonizing the chronology or identifying the image definitively.
Retain us and ancestors, slavery’s house image, visible signs and protection in both journey and human surroundings.
Preserve the unsettling cannot and will-not-forgive statements, without adding qualifiers to soften them.
Keep the condition, reversal from good to harm and threatened destruction as Joshua’s warning.
Retain gods among the present people rather than recasting them as only ancestral temptations.
Keep the scroll’s title distinct from Moses’ instruction in chapter 23, and retain the tree and sanctuary without relocating them.
Preserve the stone’s hearing, shift from us to you and witness language rather than replacing personification with an explanation.
Keep the bones’ journey, purchased plot, full seller relationship and untranslated uncertain money unit.
Preserve lineage and grant to the son while retaining the hill-name’s geographical and personal senses.
